clauses.section: Actors
clauses.text: **Pilot** — performs E1, E2, E3, E4.

clauses.section: Actors
clauses.text: **Another ship** — performs nothing.

clauses.section: Actors
clauses.text: **The game** — performs E5.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: *You open the page. A world exists, you are in a ship in it, and the controls answer. Nothing else in the game can happen until this does.*

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: Begins when: the page is open and nothing has started. Is finished when: the pilot is flying and in control.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: **UC-E1-1 — The page builds a world to fly in.** Runs when: the page is open and nothing has started. Leaves true: a world exists to fly in. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: Opening the page constructs a WebGL renderer and a scene. Until this exists there is no space, no ship, nothing to look at.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: Rests on: `renderer`, `scene`, `EXPOSURE`.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: with WebGL unavailable the page reports it rather than showing a blank canvas

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: the renderer is constructed exactly once per page load

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: **UC-E1-2 — The game gives the pilot a ship.** Runs when: a world exists to fly in. Leaves true: the pilot has a ship in that world. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: A ship is built for the player and placed in the world with a hull, a texture and a collision radius.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: Rests on: `makeShip`, `SHIP_TEX`, `SHIP_R`.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: ships[0] exists with role 'player' after load

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: the ship has a non-zero collision radius, so it can be hit

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: **UC-E1-3 — The simulation advances every frame.** Runs when: the pilot has a ship in that world. Leaves true: the simulation is stepping. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: A frame loop runs, clamps the timestep so a stalled tab cannot teleport the world, and steps the simulation.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: Rests on: `frame`, `step`.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: a frame gap longer than 50ms is clamped rather than integrated whole

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: pausing and resuming the tab does not move the ship

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: **UC-E1-4 — The pilot's controls move the ship.** Runs when: the simulation is stepping. Leaves true: the controls answer the pilot. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: Thrust, yaw and pitch answer the keyboard, bounded by drag and a maximum speed, so the ship is flyable rather than merely present.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: Rests on: `THRUST`, `DRAG`, `VMAX`, `YAW_RATE`, `PITCH_RATE`.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: holding thrust raises speed until it plateaus at VMAX, not beyond

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: releasing thrust decays speed rather than stopping dead

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: **UC-E1-5 — The pilot can see where the ship is going.** Runs when: the controls answer the pilot. Leaves true: the pilot is flying and in control. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: A chase camera trails the ship, leads it slightly, and lags rather than snapping, so the pilot has a usable frame of reference.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: Rests on: `CAM_BACK`, `CAM_AHEAD`, `CAM_LAG`, `CAM_UP`.

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: the camera sits behind and above the ship at rest

clauses.section: E1 — Arrive and fly
clauses.text: a hard turn moves the camera smoothly, with no instantaneous jump

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: *You fly a small ship at some rocks. You shoot one, it breaks, and the pieces are worth something. You scoop them up and the bar at the bottom fills. When it fills, you are owed something.*

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: Begins when: the pilot is flying and in control. Is finished when: the pilot is owed at least one upgrade point.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: **UC-E2-1 — The system populates a belt with rocks.** Runs when: the pilot is flying and in control. Leaves true: a belt of rocks exists. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: A mining belt is seeded with instanced asteroids, capped so the field is dense without becoming thousands of draw calls.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: Rests on: `makeMiningBelt`, `spawnAsteroid`, `AST_MAX`, `AST_KEEP`, `ROCK_POOLS`.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: the field holds rocks up to AST_MAX and never more

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: rocks are drawn from instanced pools, not one mesh each

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: **UC-E2-2 — The system finds the rocks near the pilot cheaply.** Runs when: a belt of rocks exists. Leaves true: a rock is within reach. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: A spatial hash rebuilt every few frames answers 'what is near me' without scanning the field, which is what makes a belt of thousands testable every frame.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: Rests on: `AST_CELL`, `AST_GRID_EVERY`.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: collision testing does not scan every rock each frame

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: a rock marked gone is skipped by the near-query rather than returned

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: **UC-E2-3 — The pilot breaks a rock apart.** Runs when: a rock is within reach. Leaves true: gems are loose in the world. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: A rock that takes enough damage is destroyed, splitting into smaller children carrying a fraction of its size and a kick outward.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: Rests on: `destroyAsteroid`, `AST_SPLIT_MIN`, `AST_SPLIT_MAX`, `AST_CHILD_FRAC`, `AST_SPLIT_KICK`.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: a destroyed rock above the no-split size yields between AST_SPLIT_MIN and AST_SPLIT_MAX children

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: the children move apart rather than sitting inside each other

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: **UC-E2-4 — Broken rock leaves gems in the world.** Runs when: gems are loose in the world. Leaves true: a gem can be picked up. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: The pieces spawn as physical gem pickups whose credit value scales with the size of the rock they came from, and which expire if nobody takes them.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: Rests on: `spawnGem`, `GEM_CREDIT_PER_SCALE`, `GEM_LIFE`.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: a bigger rock yields gems worth more credits than a smaller one

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: an uncollected gem disappears after GEM_LIFE seconds

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: **UC-E2-5 — The pilot scoops a gem.** Runs when: a gem can be picked up. Leaves true: gem credits are in the hold. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: Flying near a gem collects it, with a magnet radius that widens as the ship is upgraded, so collection is a flight skill rather than a pixel-hunt.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: Rests on: `magnetFor`, `GEM_MAGNET`, `GEM_PICK_R`, `GEM_GRAB_R`.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: a gem inside the magnet radius moves toward the ship without an exact pass-over

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: the magnet radius grows when the relevant upgrade is bought

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: **UC-E2-6 — Collected credits bank an upgrade point.** Runs when: gem credits are in the hold. Leaves true: the pilot is owed at least one upgrade point. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: Gem credits fill a bar; each time it fills it converts into one banked upgrade point, up to a cap.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: Rests on: `gemBarAdd`, `GEM_BAR_MAX`, `GEM_BAR_RATE`, `GEM_PTS_CAP`.

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: GEM_BAR_MAX credits collected converts to exactly one banked point

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: only the player's ship banks points; an AI ship collecting gems banks none

clauses.section: E2 — Mine the belt
clauses.text: banked points stop accumulating at GEM_PTS_CAP

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: *You have a point. Put it into guns, shields or engines and get a little better now; or hold out, max everything, and trade the whole ship for a bigger frame and lose every upgrade you bought. That is the only real decision in the game.*

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: Begins when: the pilot is owed at least one upgrade point. Is finished when: the ship is measurably better than it was.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: **UC-E3-1 — The pilot spends a point on one of eight stats.** Runs when: the pilot is owed at least one upgrade point. Leaves true: at least one stat is above zero. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: A banked point goes into one of eight named stats, in flight, each capped so no single stat absorbs the whole run.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: Rests on: `spendStat`, `STAT_ORDER`, `STAT_GAIN`, `STAT_MAX`.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: spending on an unknown stat name is refused with the list of real ones

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: a stat already at STAT_MAX refuses further points rather than consuming them

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: **UC-E3-2 — Each point visibly changes how the ship performs.** Runs when: at least one stat is above zero. Leaves true: the ship is measurably better than it was. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: A stat is a multiplier the simulation actually reads, so a point spent is felt rather than merely displayed.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: Rests on: `statMult`.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: raising speed increases the ship's achieved velocity in flight

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: a stat at zero leaves its multiplier at exactly 1.0

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: **UC-E3-3 — Maxing every stat arms the trade-in.** Runs when: at least one stat is above zero. Leaves true: every stat is at its cap. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: Only when all eight stats are at their cap, with a further point banked, does the ship become eligible for the next hull.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: Rests on: `tierUpReady`, `TIER_UP`, `STAT_MAX`.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: with seven stats maxed the tier-up is not offered

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: with eight maxed and no banked point the tier-up is not offered

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: **UC-E3-4 — The game names the hull that comes next.** Runs when: every stat is at its cap. Leaves true: a next hull is on offer. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: The ladder of hulls is a fixed order, and the ship's current class determines exactly which one is on offer.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: Rests on: `nextTierHull`, `hullTierIdx`, `HULL_ORDER_ORIGINAL`.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: a ship at the top of the ladder is offered nothing

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: a generated hull is placed at its size tier's rank rather than off the ladder

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: **UC-E3-5 — Taking the new hull costs every upgrade bought.** Runs when: a next hull is on offer. Leaves true: the ship is flying a new frame. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: Accepting the trade-in swaps the frame and resets all eight stats to zero, which is what makes holding out a real decision rather than a free reward.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: Rests on: `takeTierUp`.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: after a tier-up every stat reads zero

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: refusing the tier-up leaves the current hull and stats untouched

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: **UC-E3-6 — The traded-up frame outperforms the one it replaced.** Runs when: the ship is flying a new frame. Leaves true: the ship is measurably better than it was. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: A hull class carries its own capacities, so the frame taken in the trade is materially better than the one given up even with every stat reset to zero. This is what makes the trade-in a decision rather than a punishment, and it is the beat that joins the tier-up arm back to the rest of the story.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: Rests on: `HULLS`, `shieldMaxFor`.

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: a ship one tier up, with all stats at zero, has a higher base shield capacity than a maxed ship of the tier below

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: each entry in HULLS declares its own capacities rather than inheriting one shared set

clauses.section: E3 — Spend the point, or save for the hull
clauses.text: the balance law the table states -- bigger hold means thinner armour and lower speed -- holds between adjacent tiers, so the trade is a trade and not a strict gain

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: *Your gun costs energy, so you cannot hold the trigger forever. Your shields soak the first hits and come back if you break away. When you lose, your gems spill for anyone to take and you start again small.*

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Begins when: the pilot is flying and in control. Is finished when: the pilot is flying again after dying.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: **UC-E4-1 — Firing costs energy the pilot cannot spend forever.** Runs when: the pilot is flying and in control. Leaves true: the ship can fire. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Each shot draws from a capacitor that refills over time, so sustained fire is bounded by a resource rather than by a cooldown alone.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Rests on: `capMaxFor`, `LASER_CAP_MAX`, `LASER_CAP_REGEN`, `LASER_CAP_PER_SHOT`.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: with the capacitor empty the ship cannot fire

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: breaking off refills the capacitor at LASER_CAP_REGEN per second

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: raising energyCap raises the ceiling the capacitor refills to

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: **UC-E4-2 — A shot travels a bounded distance.** Runs when: the ship can fire. Leaves true: a shot is travelling. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: A bullet leaves the muzzle at a finite speed and expires after a finite life, which is what gives the weapon a range and makes closing the distance a decision.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Rests on: `BULLET_SPEED`, `BULLET_LIFE`, `MUZZLE_OFF`.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: a bullet expires after BULLET_LIFE seconds rather than travelling forever

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: a target beyond BULLET_SPEED times BULLET_LIFE cannot be reached by a direct shot

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: **UC-E4-3 — A shot that connects damages what it hit.** Runs when: a shot is travelling. Leaves true: damage is being exchanged. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Contact applies damage, and the gun cannot fire again until the interval its own weapon type declares has passed, so damage over time is bounded by the weapon and by the pilot's investment in fireRate rather than by how fast a key is pressed.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Rests on: `BULLET_DMG`, `BULLET_R`, `WEAPONS`, `statMult`.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: a bullet passing within BULLET_R of a ship registers a hit

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: the interval between shots is the weapon's own cd from the WEAPONS table, divided by the ship's fireRate multiplier, so buying fireRate visibly shortens it

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: two weapon types with different cd values fire at visibly different rates on the same hull

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: **UC-E4-4 — Shields take the hit before the hull does.** Runs when: damage is being exchanged. Leaves true: a shield arc is down. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Damage is absorbed by a directional shield arc, each arc carrying half the ship's total shield, before any of it reaches the hull.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Rests on: `drainShield`, `shieldArcMaxFor`.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: a hit from ahead drains the forward arc and leaves the aft arc untouched

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: hull integrity does not fall while the struck arc still has charge

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: **UC-E4-5 — A ship that runs out of hull dies.** Runs when: a shield arc is down. Leaves true: the pilot's ship is destroyed. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: When damage exhausts the hull the ship is destroyed, removed from the fight, and the kill is attributed to whoever landed it.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Rests on: `killShip`, `killByShip`.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: a destroyed ship stops being a valid target

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: the killer is credited, so a kill is attributable

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: **UC-E4-6 — Death spills the cargo for anyone to take.** Runs when: the pilot's ship is destroyed. Leaves true: the hold is on the floor. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: The credits banked into the hold are dropped into the world on death, so a long uninterrupted run is worth more than the sum of its minutes.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Rests on: `spillGems`.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: a pilot dying with credits leaves collectable gems at the wreck

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: a pilot dying with nothing spills nothing

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: **UC-E4-7 — The pilot comes back small after a pause.** Runs when: the hold is on the floor. Leaves true: the pilot is flying again after dying. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: After a delay the pilot respawns without the hull they lost, which is the cost that makes the fight matter.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: Rests on: `RESPAWN_DELAY`.

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: respawn does not happen before RESPAWN_DELAY seconds have passed

clauses.section: E4 — Fight, die, and lose the cargo
clauses.text: the respawned ship is not the tier that died

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: *The session stops, and what you did survives it: the score, the ship you were flying, the state that has to be there when you come back.*

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: Begins when: the pilot is flying again after dying. Is finished when: the run is over and what happened is on record.

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: **UC-E5-1 — The game gathers what is worth keeping.** Runs when: the pilot is flying again after dying. Leaves true: a snapshot of the run exists. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: The player's ship, progress and standing are collected into one versioned snapshot.

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: Rests on: `gatherSaveState`.

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: the snapshot carries a version field, so an old save is recognisable as old

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: with no player ship the snapshot is refused rather than written empty

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: **UC-E5-2 — The snapshot is written where it can be found again.** Runs when: a snapshot of the run exists. Leaves true: the snapshot is in storage. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: The snapshot is stored under a known key in browser storage, so it survives the page closing.

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: Rests on: `SAVE_KEY`, `persist`.

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: closing and reopening the page finds the previous snapshot

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: a snapshot written under the key replaces the previous one rather than accumulating

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: **UC-E5-3 — The snapshot is kept current, not written only at the end.** Runs when: the snapshot is in storage. Leaves true: the stored snapshot is no more than one interval old. Status in the existing source: HAVE.

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: Saving runs on a cadence during play, so an unclean exit costs at most one interval rather than the whole session.

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
clauses.text: Rests on: `SAVE_INTERVAL_S`.

clauses.section: E5 — The run ends and is remembered
